# Compact message protocol between agents and subagents: plan

## GOAL
Cut the context that briefs, hand-backs, checks and plan routing add to each agent. The model writes only status, result, file references, evidence when the policy needs it, and an E flag. The hooks record everything else. The result stays measurable and works with today's parsers.

## CONTEXT (facts that shape the plan)

**Today's report and brief rules**
- `dot-claude/rules/claude-agent-stack.md:34-48` "Briefs and hand-backs":
  - `:38` is the clean-finish header (`<input> · <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · <type>`).
  - `:39-46` is the STATUS/RESULT/EVIDENCE/FILES/NEXT block.
  - `:47` sets the caps by role (~1,000 / ~2,500 chars).
  - `:48` says that no STATUS line means a clean finish.
  - `:51` makes builders run `; date '+%F %R'`, only so they can write the timestamp.
  - `:53` is the evidence-gated round-trip rule.
- The prompt budget only allows displacement. Rules may be at most 0.95 × 12,198 (`tests/prompt_budget.py:96-97`). Agent bodies may be at most 0.867 × base. The BlackCat body is capped at 5,200 (`:50`).

**What the hooks already know**
- The registry `agents/<id>.json` already records type, depth, parent, spawned, started and stopped (`agent_guard.py:108-110`). It is written at SubagentStart (`:3247-3289`) and SubagentStop (`:3343-3347` → `mark_stopped` `:3323-3340`).
- The ledger `spawns/<tid>.json` records by, type, task, ts and status (`:2000-2243`).
- Tokens, wall time, tool counts and `status_code` per segment come from `stack_usage.py` (columns at `:91-105`).
- In this session, the result of a foreground Agent call already ended with `agentId: …` and `<usage>subagent_tokens / tool_uses / duration_ms</usage>` (I saw it on my own claude-code-guide call). The model never needs to write the id, type, time, duration or tokens.

**What hooks can and cannot do** (claude-code-guide, hooks.md, read 2026-10-03)
- SubagentStart `additionalContext` is supported.
- SubagentStop input has `last_assistant_message` and `stop_hook_active`. `decision:"block"` plus a reason keeps the subagent running and gives it the reason. SubagentStop cannot modify the final message.
- PostToolUse(Agent): `tool_response` has `content`, `agentId`, `totalTokens` (final request only), `totalDurationMs` and `totalToolUseCount`. `additionalContext` reaches the parent. `updatedToolOutput` "works for all tools", but the Agent tool is not named (unverified).
- Background children (all of BlackCat's) return a completion notification. No hook is documented that can see or rewrite it. So the format must be enforced at the source (SubagentStop), not at the parent.

**JSON mode**
- `REPORT_JSON_LINE` is injected at SubagentStart and SessionStart only when `STACK_REPORT_FORMAT=json` (`agent_guard.py:3292-3320`, `:3411-3436`).
- `settings.json:650-660` wires SubagentStop to agent_guard (timeout 15 s).

**Status parsers that must stay compatible**
- `stack_usage.py:154-155`: `^STATUS:\s*(done|partial|blocked)`, codes 0/1/2. A last text message with no STATUS line counts as 0 ("clean", `:486-497`).
- `stack_limits.py:718-721, 883-888` uses `status_code` 0/1 to decide which limit hits were "tight".
- `stack-tree:296`: a lenient regex. No STATUS line shows as "done" (`:374-376`, `:584-585`).
- `stack_sdk.py:12-50` `parse_report`: clean, status, json and text forms; FILES split on `,` or newline.
- Frozen baseline: `compute_stats.py:180-181` and `collect_b0v2.py:52`. COMPARE.md §0 says a changed definition means a schema bump plus recomputing BEFORE from the frozen inputs.

**Baseline numbers** (`stats_before.md`)
- Compliance with the current rule: new_install 21/24 and 12/13; old_install 16/40 (`:17-19`).
- Deviations include `header_template_literal` and `header_agent_mismatch` (`:124`), so model-written headers do go wrong.
- Overclaim 3/40, underclaim 1/40 (`:119`).
- No cost field exists. BEFORE has one orchestrated run (old_install).

**Other constraints**
- Read gate: anything under `.claude-work/` is never gated (`read_gate.py:25, 288-295`), so huge output files there are read in full with no warning.
- Planner, code-reviewer, plan-reviewer, verifier, security-auditor and proof-checker cannot write files (no Write tool, or Bash held to read-only commands). Their findings and plans have to come back inline.
- `orchestrator.md:25-27` already keeps `plan.md` as a DAG of at most 32 tasks and uses Agent descriptions like `T3 …`. `stack_usage.py:141,564-567` already pulls the node id out of descriptions, so routing by node is measurable today.

## REQUIREMENTS / NON-GOALS

**Requirements**
- R1. The model writes only STATUS (done|partial|failed|blocked), an optional E flag, RESULT, FILES (path and purpose), EVIDENCE when the policy needs it, and NEXT.
- R2. Hooks record id, type, start, stop, duration, tool uses, report size and file metadata. When a report is valid, nothing is added to the parent's context.
- R3. Evidence is always kept for partial, failed and blocked. Evidence longer than 5 lines goes to a file and is referenced.
- R4. Files travel only as references. The hook stamps size and sha8 and flags files that do not exist.
- R5. Briefs use the keys GOAL / IN / C / DONE / OUT, pass references only, and never chain context.
- R6. Check verdicts are compact.
- R7. `plan.md` is a DAG and routing goes by node id.
- R8. Caps, a pasted-blob detector, one restate at most, and fail-open on any error.
- R9. Old and new formats parse side by side.
- R10. Report and brief sizes are logged so the saving can be measured.
- R11. The prompt budget does not grow.

**Non-goals**
- User-facing reply style (the Output economy rule stays as it is).
- A role-aware split of the rules file, or SubagentStart injection of role blocks.
- Caps on BlackCat's replies to you.
- Aligning permission vocabulary.
- Rewriting the parent-visible tool result in v1.
- Changing the SDK JSON schema beyond adding `failed` and `eflag`.
- Editing the frozen `stats_before/`.

Optional later (no tasks): rules split with per-role SubagentStart blocks; caps on BlackCat's replies; vocabulary alignment; truncating results with PostToolUse(Agent) `updatedToolOutput` after a probe; dropping the "Started …" line once no format needs it.

## PROTOCOL SPEC (answers to design questions 1–9)

### (1) The report: who writes what

**Hook-written, never model-written:**
- agent id and type: event, registry
- start, stop and duration: registry `started`/`stopped`; `totalDurationMs` for foreground calls
- tool uses: `totalToolUseCount`
- tokens per run: the stack_usage collector (`tool_response.totalTokens` covers only the final request, so it is not used)
- file size and sha8
- report chars, format and restate count

These go to the registry `report` field and to `usage/reports.jsonl`, which holds no text. The ledger row shows the status and the report path. Nothing is injected into the parent: the foreground result frame already carries the id and usage, and background notifications cannot be hooked.

**Model-written grammar.** It keeps the existing `STATUS:` prefix and keys so every current regex still matches. It adds `failed` and the E flag. The clean-finish header and the `date` call are dropped.

~~~
report      := status_line NL "RESULT: " text [NL files] [NL evidence] [NL next]
status_line := "STATUS: " ("done"|"partial"|"failed"|"blocked") [" · E:" ("look"|"drop")]
files       := "FILES:" (NL "- " path [" — " purpose≤60])+
evidence    := "EVIDENCE: " (inline ≤ 5 lines | "→ " path[":" a "-" b])
next        := "NEXT: " (agent ": " step | "ASK USER: " question " (" options ")")
~~~

**Rules per status**
- done: RESULT is required. FILES if any file was created or changed. EVIDENCE and the E flag only under the evidence policy.
- partial, failed or blocked: EVIDENCE and NEXT are required, and E:look is implied. The validator sets it if it is missing.
- Empty fields are left out.

**Examples (illustrative, not real outputs)**

1. Success
~~~
STATUS: done
RESULT: stack_usage accepts failed/ok; status_code domain unchanged; tests pass (pytest -q tests/test_stack_usage.py).
FILES:
- dot-claude/hooks/stack_usage.py — STATUS_RE, STATUS_CODE
~~~

2. Failed, with evidence
~~~
STATUS: failed · E:look
RESULT: Restate guard not applied: SubagentStop blocks twice for one run.
EVIDENCE: uv run pytest -q tests/test_agent_guard.py -k restate → 1 failed
  AssertionError: decision 'block' emitted twice for run a1
NEXT: main-coder: key the restate marker by the registry `started` stamp
~~~

3. Success, with justifying evidence (brief said `ev:req`, a hooks trigger fired)
~~~
STATUS: done · E:drop
RESULT: .claude-work exemption narrowed to ≤ 256 KB; knob READ_GATE_CLAUDE_WORK_BYTES (0 = old behaviour).
FILES:
- dot-claude/hooks/read_gate.py — gated(), KNOBS
EVIDENCE: → .claude-work/compact/out/T5.ev.txt (self-test and pytest output)
~~~

**Hard caps on model-written chars.** The table lives in the new `stack_report.py`. The numbers are provisional and get recalibrated from observe-mode data before enforcement.

| class | agents | cap |
|---|---|---|
| lookup | oracle, scout, explore, claude-code-guide | 1,000, hard |
| builder (default) | every other agent with Write | 800 on done, 2,500 otherwise, hard |
| coord | orchestrator | 2,500, hard (summary of at most 10 lines plus refs) |
| review | code-reviewer, plan-reviewer, security-auditor, verifier, proof-checker | 6,000, soft (logged only; findings are the deliverable and must stay inline) |
| plan | planner | 12,000, soft (logged only) |

**Compatibility**
- `STATUS_RE` in stack_usage and stack-tree matches the prefix, and `· E:x` comes after the status word.
- `parse_report` takes the first token of the status line. It needs: an `eflag` key, `failed`, and stripping of `- ` and ` — purpose` from FILES.
- stack_usage maps `failed`→1 and `ok`→0. The domain {0,1,2} stays, so learned limits keep their meaning. The exact status is kept in `reports.jsonl`.
- stack-tree prefers the validated `registry.report.status`.
- The §13 SUBAGENTS.md reads the registry `report` (status, eflag, files with size and sha8, verdict and counts, report path) instead of regex excerpts. So §14 should land before §13.
- Baseline: the AFTER compute script bumps the schema to 1.2.0 (the regex adds failed/ok, `format_class` adds `compact`) and recomputes BEFORE from the same frozen inputs, as COMPARE.md §0 requires.

### (2) Evidence policy
- Always present for partial, failed and blocked, always with E:look.
- On done, only when one of these holds:
  - the brief says `ev:req`;
  - a review trigger fired (rules `:52`), which counts as `ev:req`;
  - the agent judges that a claim needs it (a deviation, an assumption, a non-obvious number).
- E:look means the parent must read the evidence before acting or relaying.
- E:drop means proof-of-work kept for reviewers or the user. The parent forwards the reference and does not read it.
- More than 5 lines go to `./.claude-work/<job>/out/<node>.ev.txt` and are referenced. Read-only agents, and any agent in Plan mode, keep evidence inline within their cap.
- The validator copies the full report text to `<state>/<sid>/reports/<agent_id>.md` (mode 0600), so a restate never loses anything.
- Evidence-gated rounds are unchanged (rules `:53`, review-protocol `:11-12`). A ping-back cites `path:line` or the EVIDENCE reference. Reviewers re-run proofs when a report has none.

### (3) Files
- The model writes `path — purpose`. The hook resolves each path against the event `cwd` and records size and sha8, or flags it missing (missing means a claimed file was hallucinated).
- Safety of that check: regular files only (`S_ISREG`), open with `O_NONBLOCK`, hash only files up to 8 MB (else size and mtime), at most 20 paths, 2 s total.
- Location: `./.claude-work/<job>/out/<node>.<ext>`, or `out/<type>-<slug>.<ext>` when there is no plan.
- Consumers read parts with Read `offset`/`limit`, `rg -n … | head`, `jq '.k'`, or `sed -n 'a,bp'`.
- Enforcement:
  - The blob detector (below) runs on the report.
  - The read gate is narrowed: under `.claude-work/`, only regular text files up to `READ_GATE_CLAUDE_WORK_BYTES` (default 262,144) skip the gate. Larger ones get the usual first-read refusal, and an identical retry passes.
- Blob detector (in `stack_report.blob_score`), any one of:
  - 10 or more lines that look like Read output (`^\s*\d+\t`);
  - a code fence over 15 lines or 1,500 chars (reviewers' diff hunks are allowed);
  - a run of base64 or hex of 200 chars or more;
  - control or binary characters;
  - any line over 2,000 chars.

### (4) Briefs and requests
~~~
GOAL: <node id> · <one line>
IN: plan.md#T3 (<path>); <dep out refs>; <file:line anchors>
C: <constraints: owned files, no-push, stdlib…>
DONE: <objective check command>
OUT: hand-back [ev:req] [file: ./.claude-work/<job>/out/T3.<ext>]
USER: <user's prompt verbatim>     # only when a prompt is forwarded verbatim (BlackCat); exempt from the cap
~~~
- Cap: 2,000 agent-written chars. It is soft: PreToolUse(Agent) logs `brief_chars` in the ledger and adds an `additionalContext` warning above the cap, or when the brief contains a pasted report or blob (`^STATUS:` lines, the hand-back frame, a blob score above the threshold). It never denies.
- No chaining: a child gets its DAG row, `plan.md#T<n>`, and the `out` references of its dependencies. It never gets the plan's text, the parent's conversation or sibling reports.
- Follow-ups go by SendMessage to the same agent id, with the same keys and only the delta.
- BlackCat is just one parent and uses the same keys (`USER:` plus references).

### (5) Checks and reviews
- STATUS is the review task's completion; the VERDICT goes in RESULT.
- Clean pass: `STATUS: done` and `RESULT: VERDICT pass — ran: <cmds>`.
- Otherwise:
  - `STATUS: done · E:look`
  - `RESULT: VERDICT pass-with-fixes|fail · <n> CRITICAL <n> HIGH <n> MEDIUM <n> LOW (plans: <n> BLOCKING)`
  - then `ASSUMED:`, `FINDINGS:` (`- [SEV] path:line — defect | evidence | proof | fix`) and `NOT CHECKED:`. These stay inline because the reviewers are read-only.
- The hook saves the copy at `reports/<id>.md`, which becomes the findings file. The orchestrator sends `apply F1,F3 from <path>` and never re-pastes the findings.
- A review that could not finish is `partial` with EVIDENCE.
- The validator extracts the verdict and the counts into `reports.jsonl`.

### (6) Plan exposition and routing
- `plan.md` rows: `| T<n> | task | owner | deps | in | done-when | status | out |`, where status is todo|running|done|partial|failed|blocked.
- The planner returns its DAG inline because it cannot write. The orchestrator writes `plan.md` once and from then on routes by id:
  - Agent description `T3 <3–5 words>` (already the convention).
  - On each report, update the row's status and out.
  - Dispatch the nodes whose dependencies are done, in one message.
  - Read a child's files only for the part it merges (`orchestrator.md:27`).
- The orchestrator returns: STATUS, RESULT with at most 10 summary lines, and FILES (`plan.md` and the outputs).
- BlackCat's relay to you keeps its own style (the Relay section). It reads EVIDENCE only on E:look or a non-done status.

### (7) The guard and hook layer
- `STACK_REPORT_FORMAT` modes:
  - unset means `observe` in Phase 1: log only, never blocks, no output;
  - `compact`: observe plus restate once; becomes the default in Phase 2 if Q1 = compact;
  - `json`: today's injection plus validation of the JSON line's shape, with the same logging;
  - `off`: no validation and no logging.
- SubagentStop flow:
  1. Skip types outside `STACK_TYPES`, and skip when `last_assistant_message` is empty.
  2. Parse and check: status present and valid; non-done has EVIDENCE and NEXT; caps by class and status; blob; missing files.
  3. Record to the registry `report`, `reports/<id>.md` and `usage/reports.jsonl`.
  4. In compact mode, block once, only if: there is a hard violation, `stop_hook_active` is false, and `report.restated` is not set for this run (keyed by the registry `started` stamp). The reason is at most 400 chars: what is wrong plus the 5-line grammar.
  5. When it blocks, return before `mark_stopped`, because the agent is still running.
  6. Any exception: warn, run `mark_stopped`, and emit no decision (fail open).
- PostToolUse(Agent) on completion copies `totalDurationMs`, `totalToolUseCount` and `totalTokens` into the ledger record, for measurement only.
- Token accounting: `report_chars`, `brief_chars` and the estimate ceil(chars/3) (as in `prompt_budget.py:306-307`, labelled an estimate) go to `usage/reports.jsonl`, which joins `runs3.csv` on (session, id). No `runs.csv` schema change.

### (8) Rollout and measurement
- Phase 1: code, behaviour-neutral (observe). The user installs it and can run the optional A arm.
- Phase 2: prompts, plus `compact` as the default, plus the read gate.
- Phase 3: docs.
- Prompt migration replaces rules `:34-48` with text no longer than the old (draft below) and drops "; end the last check command with `; date '+%F %R'`" from `:51`. The BlackCat, orchestrator and planner bodies change with net ≤ 0 chars. The review-protocol skill body carries the verdict details (only its description counts toward the budget).
- Measurement: steps S9 and S10.
- Savings: "by design, not measured". Method: rewrite the 77 frozen final reports mechanically under the new rules (`stats_before/inputs/**/final_*.txt`) to get the estimated report-chars saving and the blob rate. That is an estimate with its method, never a measurement.

### (9) Risks
See RISKS below.

### Draft rules section (replaces `:34-48`; the builder measures it against the old length)
~~~
## Briefs and hand-backs
- Brief: `GOAL:` one line · `IN:` paths/URLs, the plan node (`plan.md#T3`) and its dependencies' output refs · `C:` constraints · `DONE:` the check · `OUT:` what to return, `ev:req` for evidence on success; a user's prompt goes verbatim after `USER:`. ≤ 2,000 chars besides it. Never paste files, plans, your conversation or other reports: the child sees only the brief. Follow-ups: SendMessage to the same agent, only the delta.
- Dispatch independent children in ONE message; dependent ones wait for their inputs. No spawn for work of a few tool calls or a result your very next step needs.
- Every subagent finish is this block, empty fields omitted; id, type, time, duration and tokens are hook-recorded, never written:
  STATUS: done | partial | failed | blocked [· E:look | E:drop]
  RESULT: <answer, numbers, decisions; never file contents>
  FILES: <one per line: path — purpose>
  EVIDENCE: <command + ≤ 5 lines of output, or → path>
  NEXT: <agent: step | ASK USER: question (options)>
- EVIDENCE always for partial, failed, blocked (E:look); on done only for `ev:req`, a fired review trigger or a claim that needs it (E:look: the parent must read it; E:drop: kept for review). Over 5 lines → a file in `./.claude-work/<job>/out/`.
- Caps (hook-checked, one restate): lookup 1,000 chars; builder 800 on done, 2,500 otherwise; reviews and plans carry their findings or plan. Files by reference only; read parts with offset/limit, rg or jq.
- Relay keeps status, caveats and refs; open EVIDENCE only on E:look or to act on it. NEXT: ASK USER goes up unchanged.
~~~

## OPTIONS (enforcement point)
- **A. Validate at the source: SubagentStop logs, then blocks once (chosen).** Documented. Works for background children. A violation costs the child one extra turn.
- **B. Rewrite at the parent with PostToolUse(Agent) `updatedToolOutput`.** No turn for the child, but it is unverified for the Agent tool, the output shape must match, and it cannot reach BlackCat's background notifications. Left as optional later.
- **C. Prompt only, no hook.** Free, but not enforceable or measurable. The baseline compliance of 16/40 (old_install) argues against it.

**Order and conflicts**
- §11 Plan-default (branch `plan-default` `c30b758`) shares `agent_guard.py`, `blackcat.md` (`:18` vs `:49`/`:57-58`, one 5,200-char budget), README, CONFIG, `settings.json` and `tests/lint_agents.py`. S2 and S3 start only after it merges.
- §13 compaction summary depends on the registry `report`, so §14 goes first. The read exemption in §13c is for `claude_compact_summary/`, a different folder from S5.
- §12 headless approval shares the agent_guard docstring, `LIFECYCLE`/`HANDLERS` (`:10704-10719`) and the docs. Run it serially, in either order.
- Resulting order: §11 → S0–S2, S4, S8 → install and A arm → S3, S5, S6, S7, S8 → §13 → §12.
- S2 does not change `settings.json`: SubagentStop is already wired at `:650-660`.

## RISKS
1. **Silent failure on success.** Mitigations: non-done always carries E:look; a fired trigger forces `ev:req`; the full report copy is kept; done reports with failure words are logged as `suspect` and measured (M7).
2. **Hallucinated success.** Mitigations: the hook checks that files exist and stamps sha8; the overclaim rate is measured against the baseline 3/40.
3. **Parsers break.** Mitigations: the `STATUS:` prefix and keys are kept; old and new formats parse side by side; the cross-parser fixture test (S4); the `status_code` domain is unchanged.
4. **Restate loops, cost, registry corruption.** Mitigations: at most one restate per run; `stop_hook_active` respected; fail open; observe mode first; no `mark_stopped` while blocked (tested).
5. **Hook timeout on model-supplied paths.** Mitigations: `S_ISREG`, `O_NONBLOCK`, 8 MB hash cap, at most 20 paths, 2 s budget.
6. **Evidence-gated rounds starved.** Mitigations: `ev:req` on fired triggers; reviewers re-run proofs (review-protocol `:11`).
7. **Prompt budget.** Mitigations: displacement measured in S3; BlackCat has ~13 chars of headroom (unverified).
8. **Secrets in saved report copies.** Mitigations: 0600 in the state dir (Edit denied at `settings.json:282`, pruned after 3 idle days); `reports.jsonl` holds no text; stack-tree keeps redacting.
9. **`SubagentHandback` (auto mode, v2.1.271+) puts the report in that tool's input.** Then `last_assistant_message` is only a note, so the validator skips (fails open) when the message is short and the last tool call is `SubagentHandback`. Unverified; the stack does not use auto mode.
10. **Plan mode or read-only agents cannot write `out/` files.** Mitigation: inline within caps, with soft caps for review and plan.
11. **Caps too tight.** Mitigation: calibrate from observe-mode data and the counterfactual distribution (S9a) before turning on `compact`.

## VERIFY
- S2/S4 tests; `agent_guard.py --self-test`; `read_gate.py --self-test`; `prompt_budget.py --check`; lint_agents; full pytest compared with the `NEXT_STEPS.md:217` baseline; install_smoke.
- S8 reviews (triggers: hooks, untrusted input, a diff over 300 lines).
- S10 real-session check.
- S9 numbers count as measured only under COMPARE.md §6: the interval excludes 0, or McNemar p < 0.05, with n stated.

## QUESTIONS
- **Q1.** Validator default after Phase 2: `compact` (restate once on a violation; recommended) or `observe` (log only)?
- **Q2.** Run an A arm of 5 or more orchestrated prompts on the Phase-1 install, with the old prompts? It costs a campaign. Without it, M5 cannot be measured, because BEFORE has one orchestrated run. Yes or no.
- **Q3.** Narrow the read gate's `.claude-work/` exemption to files of at most 256 KB? Recommended yes, with knob value 0 keeping today's behaviour.
- **Q4.** Should read-only reviewers and the planner keep returning findings and plans inline (recommended for v1), or get Write limited to `.claude-work/**/out/`? The second is a guard and permission change and needs a security review.
